title: Macy's Big Parade Turns 100 — a Little Late, but Bigger Than Ever
summary:
New York's most famous parade is turning 100. The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade was first planned for Thursday, November 26, but strong winds and the chance of flooding pushed it to Saturday, November 28. It is the first time the parade has ever been put off, and safety worries about the giant balloons also played a part.

The good news is that the show is still on, and it is bigger than ever. It airs live at 8:30 a.m. ET on NBC and Telemundo, and it streams on Peacock. Parade leaders say 95% of the acts will still perform on Saturday. Two marching bands cannot make it, but LL Cool J and Gloria Gaynor will join as surprise guests.

This year has a record 100 giant balloons, with new ones of Bluey, Hello Kitty, Mickey Mouse and Underdog. RAYE opens the music, and stars like Queen Latifah and Teddy Swims will perform. Megan Hilty will honor Dolly Parton, and Savannah Guthrie, Hoda Kotb and Al Roker will host. Some services offer free trials, so check the weather news first.
why_it_matters: If you love parades, giant balloons, and music, this is a fun holiday show you can watch with your family at home.
